items.title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
OpenAI updates ChatGPT to handle complex everyday questions, web searches, and images more reliably
items.excerpt: OpenAI is making GPT-6.2 Sol the new default model in ChatGPT's chat tab, rolling it out worldwide. In internal tests, image understanding jumped from 47.4 to 71.7 percent, and the model now handles difficult instructions correctly 78.1 percent of the time. It also sticks to safety policies more consistently. The article OpenAI updates ChatGPT to handle complex everyday questions, web searches, and images more reliably appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy
items.excerpt: Since May, SpaceXSI has been renting compute to competitors like Anthropic and Google while scaling back its own AI projects. Anthropic pays about $3.1 billion a month, Google $800 million, the New York Times reports. After its June IPO, SpaceXSI disbanded the 60-person Grok Imagine team, among other cuts. The article Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits
items.excerpt: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has released internal perplexity scores for the entire GPT series for the first time, up to an unreleased model beyond the current generation. The metric shows that core capabilities emerge at surprisingly precise thresholds. Pachocki is pushing to make perplexity an industry-wide progress metric and establish shared limits before control over AI behavior erodes. The article OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits appeared first on The Decoder .
